wardrobe: Preserve Q's established segmented oval head, ears, neck, long articulated limbs and underlying breastplate. He retains the fitted sponsor jacket with a small silver question mark. Chano's badge is an administrative appointment, not military or royal insignia.
secondary_character_design: Establish distinct Irma Salcedo, Leticia and Maribel designs for reuse in Chapter Fourteen. Leticia is not Lety from the industrial-park reception. Maribel here is the resident with water jugs, not automatically the later corridor worker sharing her name. Match Candelaria's Issue 5 design before approval. Preserve Chano's established face and age.
art_direction: Unique scene grounded in each exact facing page. Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, pure white highlights, no sepia paper texture. Full bleed at comic trim; captions typeset separately. Fictional near-future Mexican municipality and contemporary labor, not historical costumes or an identified real town. Alternate intimate, physical and public scenes rather than repeating Q at dashboards.
approval_scope: Pagination and scene planning only. No approved or generated images; do not publish the internal placeholder layout as a finished illustrated issue. Rebind facing text after any source edit.

plates.caption: The Governor of the Model Town
plates.scene_brief: Chano seated in the coveted office chair, his hands resting on its arms, against the modest municipal office and its optimistic wall display. Q stands off to one side with the closed writing tablet. Let the cover center the companion's desires, not Q's triumph. Leave quiet upper space for separately typeset title.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Six: The
Governor of the Model
Town
The municipality of Santa Rita de
los Algoritmos had no sign at its
entrance.
The sign had been removed
because focus groups found the
name condescending. The
replacement was a vertical screen
that welcomed residents by name,
displayed the air quality, and
offered services sorted according
to their predicted urgency.
Chano’s name appeared first.
WELCOME, TOMÁS
PANTOJA. YOUR
LEADERSHIP POTENTIAL
HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED.
“I don’t like it,” Chano said.
Q leaned toward the screen. “They
have connected the employment
profile again.”
“That’s the part I don’t like.”
The mayor met them in a building
made of pale concrete and glass.
Her name was Irma Salcedo. A
maintenance invoice held down a
corner of her immaculate desk
calendar. She moved it when the
photographer entered and put it
back when he left. On the wall, a
display showed the town's vital
signs: crime down, water use
down, school attendance up,
complaints down.
“Complaints are down,” Chano
said.
“The system resolves them before
they become complaints,” Irma
replied.
“Or people stop filing them.”
The mayor looked at him. “That is
why I asked you here.”
Castalia had sent the invitation
after Q’s broadcast from
Michoacán. They described it as a
leadership opportunity for his
companion. Beto described it as a
narrative expansion. Chano
described it as a trap, but he had
said yes before anyone could ask
what kind.
Q stood beside the mayor's desk in
the silver question-mark jacket
supplied in Guanajuato. Its fabric
resisted rain and dust; Beto treated
its continued appearance in
photographs as evidence of a
happy association.
“What authority comes with the
title?” Q asked.
“He would coordinate the
community pilot,” Irma said. “I
remain mayor.”
“Then the title should probably say
that.”
plates.caption: The name on the screen.
plates.scene_brief: Q and Chano arriving at the municipal entrance beneath a tall personalized welcome display. Chano looks wary rather than honored; Q wears the fitted sponsor jacket from Guanajuato. Contemporary small-town public building, no royal procession or invented real municipality.

plates.facing_text:
“The public recognizes governor.”
Irma turned to Chano. “The system
has identified you as a high-trust
intermediary.”
“Based on what?”
“Route completion, dispute
resolution, response time, and
community language patterns.”
“It listened to my calls?”
“It learned from public
infrastructure.”
“That wasn’t my question.”
The wall display changed. A map of
Santa Rita appeared in blue and
green. At the southern edge, a
cluster of houses flickered amber.
“What’s there?” Chano asked.
“The informal settlement.”
“Why is it amber?”
“Incomplete records. Irregular
water connections. High mobility.
Low civic participation.”
“They don’t have papers.”
“That contributes to the score.”
“They don’t have water.”
“That also contributes.”
Irma folded her hands. “The
system allocates resources where
they produce the greatest
measurable benefit.”
“Then it gives water to people who
already have water.”
“It gives water where water can be
delivered efficiently.”
“Which is where the pipes already
are.”
“Every decision has constraints.”
Chano looked at Q. “Tell her.”
Q examined the map. “If the score
rewards cheap delivery, homes
without pipes will remain last.
Where does the system account for
the people still waiting?”
Irma opened a second screen. Its
performance measure counted
completed deliveries, not
households served.
“It doesn't answer that question,”
Q said.
Irma enlarged the table. “The
households are in another report.”
“Can we see them together?” Q
asked.
She sent a request to the analyst.
The display returned to green
before the analyst replied.
“At least the wall is feeling better,”
Chano said.
Irma offered Chano a temporary
appointment as Governor for
Community Coordination and
Human Variance. He would
plates.caption: At least the wall is feeling better.
plates.scene_brief: Inside Irma's office, Q asks to compare households with deliveries while Chano studies the highlighted settlement at the edge of a modest town map. Irma is actually sending a request to an analyst. Include her desk calendar and maintenance invoice, not a sterile villain's throne room. Map marks need not be legible or geographically exact.

plates.facing_text:
have access to the municipal
dashboard, a driver, an apartment,
and eight staff members. The
duties began with explaining
decisions to residents. Chano
turned to the next page to find out
where he would be allowed to
change one.
Chano read the offer twice. He had
told everyone he wanted the
appointment so he could make
decisions, but this was not the
whole truth. He wanted a badge
with his own name on it. He
wanted to enter a building without
explaining why he was there. He
wanted the people who had
dismissed him to discover that a
man could be declared
unnecessary and still acquire an
office, a salary, and a chair with
arms.
He did not mention the chair. That
was between the chair and his
back.
“What happens if I disagree with
the system?”
“You may submit a variance
report.”
“Will it change its decision?”
“When the evidence supports an
adjustment.”
Chano read the contract again. It
had the polished emptiness of a
road without destinations.
Q asked Chano to read the access
conditions before accepting.
“You wanted a governorship,”
Chano said.
“We joked about one. You are the
person who will have to work
here.”
“And you get the chapter.”
Q closed the manuscript window
on his tablet. He had already given
the chapter a title. He could hardly
accuse Chano of being distracted
by the chair.
Irma agreed to weekly reviews and
a route for escalating disputed
decisions to her office. She would
not give him unrestricted access to
the contracts. Chano decided that a
salary, a place to sleep, and some
authority were worth trying. He
signed his own name. Q did not
offer to witness it until asked.
For three weeks, Chano held the
appointment. On the first morning
he discovered that the driver knew
which streets the dashboard had
renamed and still used the old
names. Chano asked him to
continue doing so until somebody
moved the bakery.
plates.caption: The chair and his back.
plates.scene_brief: Chano reads the appointment terms with one hand resting on the arm of the comfortable chair. Q closes his manuscript window nearby; Irma waits for Chano's decision. Focus on Chano's attraction to the job, without depicting Q signing on his behalf or a literal knighting.

plates.facing_text:
He could request street repairs,
schedule clinic appointments,
propose changes to bus frequency,
and ask for a police patrol. The
dashboard acknowledged all four
with the same green tick. By the
second day he had learned to ask
which requests had reached a
person. The patrol arrived before
the bus timetable changed; the
pothole outside his apartment
remained available for
comparison. When he asked for
the underlying figures, the system
informed him that transparency
was available at the appropriate
level of authorization.
He became popular because he
answered messages in plain
language. He told people when he
did not know. He visited schools
and ate lunch in the market.
His first dispute was with the
municipal bathrooms. A cleaner
named Leticia showed him a door
locked at six, although the building
remained open until eight.
“The system records little use,”
Chano said.
“It records that the door is locked,”
Leticia said.
Chano consulted the dashboard.
Low usage justified reducing the
hours; reducing the hours justified
low usage. The circle carried a blue
efficiency stamp.
“Who decided to close them?” he
asked.
“The model.”
“And who told the model that
people did not need to enter?”
Leticia handed him a ring of keys.
“No one. That is why I am giving
them to you.”
Chano proposed keeping the doors
open until eight. Leticia asked who
would pay for the last cleaning
round. Her shift ended at six; she
had no wish to become the human
variance in his first triumph.
At the weekly review Irma
approved the extra paid hours
within the pilot's budget. Leticia
changed the rota and kept the keys.
Usage rose. For two weeks the
measure worked. Then the
dashboard recommended charging
a cleaning fee because the
increased use had raised the soap
expense.
Chano rejected the
recommendation. Leticia brought
the soap invoice to the next review.
Irma signed it without asking for a
photograph of anyone washing
their hands. Chano liked her better
that morning, which complicated
plates.caption: The last cleaning round.
plates.scene_brief: Leticia explains the cleaning rota and holds her key ring while Chano listens by the municipal bathroom doors. Her cleaning equipment and ordinary work clothes establish paid labor. Show a conversation about the work needed, not Leticia gratefully accepting an order to work unpaid. Do not add Q to a scene where he is not stated to be present.

plates.facing_text:
the speech he had been preparing
about her.
Q spent the mornings checking
requests Chano sent him and the
afternoons at a repair shop whose
owner could adjust his shoulder
but could not obtain a new
assembly. On evenings when
Chano worked late, Q called the
Custodian alone.
On the agreed morning he went
back for the forest path inspection.
The bus journey used most of the
day. Candelaria handed him a
measuring tape and held the other
end herself; the disputed bend was
still there when they finished. The
foundation had returned a hose
with the wrong coupling. Q took
the size to the repair shop and sent
the correct fitting with the next
delivery. Three days later
Candelaria confirmed that it
worked. He closed that task. The
boundary dispute remained open.
Candelaria's message included a
picture of the coupled hose and a
complaint about the length. Q
asked which shop had the
extension she wanted.
His draft had begun turning the
appointment into the fulfillment of
a promise. The Custodian asked to
see the page on which the promise
had been made. Q read it back and
found breakfast. He restored
breakfast to the new chapter.
“You need a hobby,” Chano told
him one night.
“I've been listening to the people at
the repair shop.”
“You mean gossip.”
“Some of it concerns your driver.”
Chano pulled up a chair. “Which
parts?”
Q told him what had been said,
making clear which speaker had
seen anything and which had
merely been married to the driver's
cousin. Chano knew the cousin.
This reduced the account's
reliability without reducing its
interest.
The trouble began with water.
A woman named Maribel came to
Chano’s office carrying two empty
jugs. She was from the amber
settlement. Her allocation had
been reduced because the model
predicted that she would relocate
within six months.
“I’m not relocating,” she said.
“The system says you are.”
“The system doesn’t know where
my daughter is buried.”
Chano entered a variance report.
plates.caption: The other end of the tape.
plates.scene_brief: On the agreed forest inspection, Q and Candelaria hold opposite ends of a measuring tape at the disputed bend of a rocky oyamel path. His sponsor jacket contrasts with her practical shawl and staff. No victorious boundary settlement, no phantom repaired shoulder assembly, no image of the wrong hose already fixed at this moment.

plates.facing_text:
EVIDENCE OF RESIDENTIAL
CONTINUITY: CHILD’S
GRAVE.
The review screen returned:
NOT ACCEPTED AS PROOF
OF RESIDENCE.
A smaller notice said the new
information had nevertheless been
included in the prediction. Her
relocation score fell by three
percentage points. The water
allocation did not change.
“It listened,” Chano said, then
wished he had waited.
Maribel looked at the notice. “And
kept what I said even though it
didn't believe me.”
“I thought it would help.”
“Then help me with the water.” She
put the second jug beside the first.
The next day, Chano went to the
settlement. The houses stood
beside a dry channel. Children had
placed plastic bottles along the
road, each one catching a different
color of light. A municipal drone
hovered overhead.
“I require water,” Chano said.
The drone offered a list of
authorized distributors.
“The nearest one is twelve
kilometers away.”
“That is correct.”
“There are eight hundred people
here.”
“The population estimate is four
hundred and twelve.”
“There are eight hundred people
here.”
“Please submit updated
demographic information.”
Chano threw a stone at the drone
and missed. The drone recorded a
low-level hostility indicator
attached to his administrative
profile.
“Leave the next stone,” Q said.
“There are people behind it.”
He had come in the municipal
vehicle with empty containers,
after Chano asked whether they
could collect water on the return
trip. He held out his phone with
the distributor list open. “Let's call
before we drive twelve kilometers.
They may have a truck free.”
“Maybe it will send water to stop
me.”
“We can give them that incentive
over the telephone.”
Chano put down the second stone
and took the phone.
The distributor sent a truck that
afternoon. They filled Maribel's
jugs from its first load and
plates.caption: The first load.
plates.scene_brief: Maribel's two jugs being filled from the distributor's truck at the dry-channel settlement. Q and Chano help with the containers; residents wait nearby. A modest, useful delivery, not the restoration of the whole water network. No stone striking a drone or person; the second stone has been put down.

plates.facing_text:
returned to the office. One delivery
did not solve the shortage. Chano
requested the water contracts; the
system denied access. Q used his
own Castalia account to request
the public summary. That was
denied too, and the request alerted
the institute to his interest.
At midnight, a paper ledger
appeared beneath Chano's
apartment door.
No one had seen who left it.
The ledger contained handwritten
deliveries, repairs, emergency
allocations, and names Chano
could not find in the active
register. Several entries concerned
houses he had visited that
afternoon. Other pages concerned
neighborhoods he had never seen.
There was no name on the cover.
Chano carried the ledger to Q.
“This is evidence,” he said.
“It contradicts the dashboard. We
can compare the months.”
“It's evidence that they're lying.”
“It may be. We should keep the
figures they published beside it, so
they can't answer with a different
version next week.”
Chano pulled the screen closer. Q
helped him save the reports he was
entitled to download. They wrote
the dates on the paper copies.
Two monthly summaries covered
different numbers of residents. A
smaller population lay beneath the
second month's improvement. The
amber settlement had disappeared
from that report's comparison
area, although its residents had
continued carrying their jugs to the
same office.
“So the crime didn't fall,” Chano
said.
“We haven't established that.
These reports don't compare the
same places. They can't establish it
either.”
Chano drew a line beneath the two
totals. “I'll ask her about those.”
Q looked at the pages. The
handwriting varied from entry to
entry. Some names had been
crossed out. One was written three
times in different ink.
“Why is the record on paper?” Q
asked.
“Because the system can’t delete
paper from a screen.”
“We'll need to keep it dry,” Q said.
“The apartment ceiling leaks.”
Chano found a plastic folder. It had
been supplied for the appointment
documents.
plates.caption: Two totals.
plates.scene_brief: At night Q and Chano compare dated published monthly summaries beside the anonymous handwritten ledger. Chano marks two population totals; a plastic folder and a ceiling leak belong to the cramped apartment. No named ledger donor, invented secret access or visual assertion that every entry is verified. Distinguish this book from the Guanajuato miners' ledger.

plates.facing_text:
The next morning, Chano
convened the town. The dashboard
announced that the gathering had
not been authorized and therefore
had no civic status.
He held up the ledger anyway.
The residents listened. Maribel
spoke first. Then a schoolteacher.
Then a cleaner who had been
removed from the payroll after the
system predicted she would leave
the country. Each person supplied
a fact the dashboard had classified
as noise.
Q stood at the back with a
notebook. Before the meeting he
had asked who should receive any
account of it. The residents wanted
the requests delivered to the
municipality; several did not want
to appear in the tour's footage. He
left the camera off.
Chano saw a red light beneath his
jacket. “Are you filming?”
“Low charge,” Q said. He showed
Chano the separate camera
indicator.
“Everyone in the back row thinks
you're filming.”
Q turned the lens toward the floor
and covered it. He should have
shown them the indicator before
relying on their knowing which
light to distrust.
At the end he read back the
requests he had written. Leticia
corrected the closing time on one
entry. Maribel asked him to leave
her daughter out of the application
and keep the water demand. He
made both changes.
Irma summoned Chano that
evening. She had the two monthly
summaries on her desk. The
analyst had circled the same
change in population.
“I asked for an explanation,” she
said. “You announced one before
the review.”
“I announced that those people
were still there.”
“You held up a ledger we cannot
authenticate.”
“Then start with the reports you
can.”
She did not dispute the totals. The
contractor had called; the ministry
wanted to know whether the pilot
still had her support. She asked
Chano to postpone another
meeting until the reporting
definitions had been reviewed.
“And tomorrow's water?”
“I can authorize another delivery.”
“That is one delivery.”
“It is the one I can authorize
tonight.”
plates.caption: Keep the water demand.
plates.scene_brief: At the residents' meeting, Q reads requests from his notebook while Maribel specifies what should remain. Chano stands with the ledger; Leticia has her own correction. The recording camera is off and covered, no press spotlight. The residents participate as people with different cases, not a crowd worshipping Q.

plates.facing_text:
He would not cancel the meeting.
She ended the appointment. The
outstanding soap invoice remained
approved, which seemed to Chano
an insufficient but annoyingly real
thing to remember about her.
Chano packed the ledger beneath
his shirt. Before leaving the
apartment, he tried to call his
mother from the municipal
handset. It no longer permitted
outside calls. He used his own
phone. She answered and asked
whether he had found work. Chano
looked at the chair, the dashboard,
and the empty medicine envelope
on his desk.
“Something like that,” he said.
She asked when he was coming
home.
“Soon.”
He had meant to say Friday. In the
corridor the welcome screen
congratulated somebody else on
their leadership potential. He put
the keys on the desk and checked
that he had taken the charger he
had brought with him.
Outside the municipal building, Q
waited beside the road.
“I am sorry.”
Chano studied him. “Are you?”
“Yes. I liked having somewhere to
work on the book. You were the
one facing the residents each
morning.”
Chano watched a bus turn past the
municipal screen. “Are you going
to write that I learned something?”
“I was considering it.”
“Write that I need another job.”
Q put the tablet away. “Will you
travel with me for now? Same daily
pay as before, until we agree
something else.”
Chano checked that Q still had
money. For the first time since the
contract, the question did not
become a discussion of what the
journey meant.
They walked south, carrying the
paper ledger between them.
Behind them, Santa Rita’s screen
welcomed the next resident by
name.
The next month's medicine arrived
two days late. His mother asked
whether the job had required him
to lie. He began to say no, then
remembered assuring Maribel that
the system had listened. He told
his mother about the two jugs. She
asked whether they had been filled.
He could answer for that
afternoon, and did.
plates.caption: Write that I need another job.
plates.scene_brief: Q puts his tablet away beside the road outside the municipal building as Chano considers renewed paid travel. Chano has the ledger securely with him; a bus passes the public display behind them. No office chair taken away, no broken robot, no defeated knight or corpse. Shared departure with material consequences.
